Presented by Elijah Fullah · 21 October 2026 · 10-minute presentation
Introduce DēGlitch and the aim of this review: moving from concept to a testable prototype — design, integration and evidence. Three headline numbers: 31 SRS IDs, 20+ UI concepts, 5 core Flutter screens.

Purpose, scope and current stage

Project aim

Help users choose and maintain a suitable VPN connection using available network conditions, device constraints and user preferences.

Current stage
Requirements baseline + broad UI design inventory + five core Flutter screens
In scope

Proposed target platforms: Android, iOS, macOS, Windows and Linux. This increment covers app-wide UI concepts, five core Flutter screens and a local-profile connectivity path; OS-specific integration is validated per platform.

Not yet claimed

No guaranteed speed gains, production-grade failover or validated adaptive/ML performance without evidence. No cross-platform support is claimed until verified on each platform.

Success means

Accurate connection state, a repeatable profile-based connection lifecycle, real diagnostics and evidence tied to requirement IDs.

About 40 s. State the aim, then the current stage. Be explicit about what is NOT yet claimed: no guaranteed speed gains, no production failover, no validated ML. The platform list is the proposed target; per REQ-PORT-001 nothing is claimed as supported until verified on that platform.

What this supports

Repeatable, controlled evidence

A local profile supports repeatable tests; peer response and bidirectional traffic were observed in a controlled test. DēGlitch status synchronization remains in refinement.

Next validation

Three checks

Repeat connection and resume tests. Bind each server row to its local profile. Replace sample metrics with real probes.

Open issues and engineering risks

Server data

Server catalogue and recommendation UI are in place; binding each entry to a matching configured profile and live ranking inputs is next.

Diagnostics

The diagnostics flow is in place; connect real probes and keep unsupported telemetry clearly marked as unavailable.

State sync

Improve status refresh and app-resume behavior; reconcile reported connection state, traffic counters and internet reachability.

Security / scope

Protect imported profile credentials and validate import, permission and failure paths. Connectivity and permission adapters need OS-specific verification.

Open SRS decisions

Platform scope, VPN protocol/library, authorized test endpoints and measurable thresholds remain open in SRS v0.2 (Appendix A) — to review with the supervisor.

About 35 s. Five items: server data binding, real diagnostic probes, state synchronization, security and per-OS verification, and the open SRS decisions that need supervisor review.
